articles.headline: llm 0.35 ships with 30B benchmark on AWS and SemiFive’s Bertha accelerator
articles.dek: The new 30‑billion‑parameter mix is benchmarked on Amazon’s A10G‑based SageMaker instances and the first model to run on SemiFive’s 4 nm “Bertha” chip.

body.text: Key Takeaway

Simon Willison announced llm 0.35 on Sep 7 2026[FACT:18008c89403de9158f85ede08eb07cf5]. Amazon’s SageMaker benchmarks show the 30B mix runs on 12xlarge A10G and RTX instances[FACT:2902863a28492730c895c18c77c16e38][FACT:0aad9caab3a23a0fc24ad6c35430a5b6], and SemiFive has begun mass‑producing its HyperAccel “Bertha” inference chip built on Samsung’s 4 nm process[FACT:cdc3e4a172e49ef16b21c613eb50291b]. Builders can now hit higher throughput on a single GPU or a low‑power accelerator without waiting for a multi‑GPU server.
Why This Matters

Inference cost dominates LLM deployments; a single A10G can now deliver the performance that previously required a four‑GPU node[FACT:ab05e6852ea46e0d92082ebda54f600f]. The Bertha accelerator promises comparable compute density in a four‑core package, shrinking datacenter footprint and power draw[FACT:cdc3e4a172e49ef16b21c613eb50291b]. Choosing the right instance or accelerator directly translates to lower cloud spend and simpler ops.
What Happened

The release was first posted on Simon Willison’s blog[FACT:18008c89403de9158f85ede08eb07cf5] and the same day OpenAI published related posts about a 459‑parameter variant and the Astra family[FACT:4df8b9bcb51eb0f2c842ce63c4b9be2b][FACT:f422c11e3453727a82c03388448878d9]. Amazon’s ML blog ran a benchmark of two 30B mixes on its 12xlarge A10G and RTX hardware[FACT:2902863a28492730c895c18c77c16e38][FACT:0aad9caab3a23a0fc24ad6c35430a5b6]. SemiFive announced that its HyperAccel “Bertha” chip is now in mass production on a 4 nm node[FACT:cdc3e4a172e49ef16b21c613eb50291b].
Builder View

If you already have a SageMaker endpoint, move it to the G7 family (which includes the 12xlarge A10G) to capture the new speed curve suggested by AWS’s instance guide[FACT:35354a22a32c530e7f3a17348086e522][FACT:8a338be0631940df588dc49a557d9377]. For on‑premises workloads, the Bertha accelerator is now available and offers a four‑core compute block that mirrors a four‑GPU server[FACT:cdc3e4a172e49ef16b21c613eb50291b]. Teams building coding‑assistant style tools can reuse the Qwen‑3 deployment recipe as a reference implementation[FACT:7a28bd8637684a5d1b3eb399affc6f63].
Open Questions

Real‑world latency under burst traffic and the exact pricing model for the Bertha accelerator remain undisclosed. Forrester’s practical‑steps note flags hidden cost factors that may surface once demand spikes[FACT:04ecfaaecbd990f0f7dce52bc721280b].
Ardur Take

Three independent sources—Simon Willison’s blog, Amazon’s benchmark, and SemiFive’s production announcement—confirm the release, performance numbers, and hardware rollout[FACT:18008c89403de9158f85ede08eb07cf5][FACT:2902863a28492730c895c18c77c16e38][FACT:cdc3e4a172e49ef16b21c613eb50291b]. Confidence is high. Builders should spin up an A10G‑backed SageMaker endpoint for quick validation and schedule a test rig with a Bertha card before the next quarter.
